## What this dashboard shows

- The Period Analysis dashboard tracks monthly financial performance across Wipro Enterprises' business units and multiple ERP systems (SAP, Oracle EBS, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Tally Prime), comparing revenue, expenses, and net income trends.
- For the latest period (2026-P007), revenue stands at ₹87.62B with expenses of ₹71.68B, generating net income of ₹18.49B across 45,177 accounting documents.
- The dashboard highlights significant month-on-month volatility, with revenue down -16.8% and expenses up +17.5% versus the prior month.

## What to report

- Revenue for 2026-P007 reached ₹87.62B, down -16.8% MoM from ₹105.27B in P006, representing a sharp reversal after the prior month's peak.
- Expenses increased to ₹71.68B (+17.5% MoM), the highest expense level in 2026 year-to-date, driving margin compression in the latest period.
- Net income for 2026-P007 was ₹18.49B, down significantly from ₹45.73B in P006, with an inventory change credit of -₹2.54B partially offsetting the decline.
- Year-over-year comparison shows 2026-P007 revenue of ₹87.62B exceeded 2025-P007 (₹81.71B) by approximately ₹6B, though 2024-P007 was lower at ₹63.16B, indicating continued growth trajectory despite monthly fluctuations.

## Watch out for

- Large inventory change swings appear in 2025 data (e.g., -₹61.89B in P003, +₹30.99B in P006, +₹23.94B in P007), creating extreme net income volatility that may reflect timing differences, system cutover issues, or data quality problems requiring investigation.
- The data includes both real SAP BDC records and simulated SAP/S/4HANA data from multiple systems, which may affect comparability and accuracy—clarify which periods contain simulated data and whether 2026 figures are audited.
- 2026-P001 shows an anomalous expense figure of only ₹23.16B (versus ₹71.26B in P002), resulting in unusually high net income of ₹73.53B—verify whether this reflects a posting error or period-end adjustment.
- The opposing trends in the latest period (revenue down, expenses up simultaneously) are unusual and warrant root-cause analysis: ask whether this reflects business reality, accrual timing, or inter-company eliminations processed in P007.
